title: sail atlas writes an atlas over several files
body:
`sail index` takes one file and writes one `.saidx`, beside the file or at `-o`. `libsail::atlas::Atlas` (sail-a59d6f) lists several indexed files in order, with a stamp and a record count for each, in a `.satlas` file. No command writes one. ## Proposal A new subcommand, separate from `sail index`: ```console $ sail atlas a.fa b.fa c.fa -o all.satlas ``` - It calls `Atlas::build`, which writes a named `.saidx` beside each input that lacks a current one and reuses the rest. It then writes the atlas to `-o`. - `-o` is required. A default named after one input would misdescribe a list of several. - One format covers every input: `--format`, or the format of the first input. An input of another format is an error. - `-` is refused, since an atlas lists paths. - It prints one line, ` records in

files listed in `. - Running it again over the same inputs is how a stale part is fixed (sail-978552). ## Rejected - `sail index` with several inputs and `-o` naming the atlas. `-o` would mean a `.saidx` path for one input and an atlas for several, and an atlas of one file could not be written. - `sail index --manifest PATH`. It keeps `-o` single-meaning but puts two outputs on one command. Splitting the commands gives each one meaning: `sail index` for one file, `sail atlas` for several. ## Cost A new subcommand. No existing command line changes.
